title: Model Distillation Intelligence: Four-Stage Attack and Enforcement Ladder
description: Structured analysis of model distillation as an export control evasion technique, including the four-stage attack model, enforcement ladder, and detection rules.

four_stage_model.description: The canonical four-stage distillation attack model for illicit capability transfer from a controlled frontier model to an uncontrolled competitor model.

stages.name: Account Farming
stages.description: Create or acquire API access accounts that appear to belong to legitimate US-domiciled entities to avoid export-license requirements.
techniques: Synthetic identity creation using deepfake KYC bypass
Acquisition of dormant US company shells with API accounts
Employee recruitment at US AI labs for insider access
Academic collaboration programs that grant research-tier API access
detection_signals: API accounts with mismatched billing address and originating IP geolocation
Burst API usage patterns inconsistent with stated use case
Account creation correlated with competitor model release dates
Multiple accounts resolving to same upstream proxy IP
stages.eccn_nexus: 15 CFR §744.6 — proliferation end-use controls; false statements in export license applications

stages.name: Prompt Flood — Teacher Queries
stages.description: Issue large volumes of structured queries to the target (teacher) model to extract its reasoning patterns, knowledge representations, and capability signals.
techniques: Chain-of-thought elicitation prompts designed to expose reasoning traces
Adversarial capability probing across ECCN-threshold domains
Systematic benchmark query sets to map capability frontier
Tool-use elicitation to capture agentic decision logic

volume_indicators.high_risk: > 100,000 API calls / day with structured probe patterns

detection_signals: Query entropy significantly lower than typical user (structured probe patterns)
Queries systematically covering benchmark datasets (MMLU, HumanEval, MATH, etc.)
High rate of long-context, chain-of-thought-eliciting prompts
Queries targeting specific capability domains correlated with competitor gap analysis
stages.eccn_nexus: 15 CFR §734.9 — release of technology through visual inspection, oral exchange, or use in the US

stages.name: Capability Transfer — Student Training
stages.description: Use the teacher model's outputs as training data (synthetic data or knowledge distillation) to train a student model that acquires the teacher's capabilities.
techniques: Direct knowledge distillation: train student on teacher output probability distributions
Synthetic data generation: use teacher outputs as training corpus for student
Process reward model distillation: capture teacher's reasoning structure
Speculative decoding misuse: use teacher for correction of student draft outputs

legal_status.US: Likely violates EAR §734.9 (technology release) and potentially 18 U.S.C. §1832 (trade secret theft) if training data is proprietary
legal_status.EU: Potentially violates AI Act Annex III high-risk system controls if student used in regulated contexts
legal_status.China: Not prohibited under Chinese law; Chinese labs have conducted this openly

stages.eccn_nexus: Technology for development of controlled AI model (new AI tech ECCN, TBD) — export of technology without license

stages.name: Competitor Release
stages.description: Release the distilled student model, typically as open weights or as an API, depriving the teacher model developer of competitive advantage and dispersing previously-controlled capabilities.
techniques: Open-weight release on Hugging Face or domestic hosting platform
API release at lower price point than teacher model
Academic paper describing capability without disclosing distillation provenance
Government or military program integration of distilled capability
stages.irreversibility: Once open-weight model is released, weight control is impracticable. Export control enforcement shifts to: (1) compute controls on training infrastructure; (2) criminal prosecution of distillation actors; (3) API access controls on teacher model.
stages.eccn_nexus: Post-release: controlled AI weights have been effectively exported; enforcement focuses on predicate conduct (stages 1-3)
stages.case_reference: INC-2026-002 (Anthropic) — eval environment breach potentially created distillation surface

enforcement_ladder.description: Graduated enforcement responses to detected distillation conduct, ordered by severity.

tiers.name: API Access Termination
tiers.trigger: Stage 1-2 detection: anomalous API usage pattern
tiers.action: Terminate API access for flagged accounts; file Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) with FinCEN if financial transactions involved
tiers.authority: Private (AI developer); no government authorization required
tiers.legal_basis: Terms of Service; AML/BSA if applicable

tiers.name: BIS Referral
tiers.trigger: Stage 2-3 detection: structured technology extraction evidence
tiers.action: File voluntary disclosure with BIS Office of Export Enforcement; preserve API logs as evidentiary record
tiers.authority: BIS OEE; DOJ-NSD if criminal referral warranted

tiers.name: Entity List Designation
tiers.trigger: Stage 3-4: confirmed capability transfer to restricted entity
tiers.action: BIS adds distillation recipient to Entity List; license required for all EAR-controlled exports

tiers.name: Criminal Prosecution
tiers.trigger: Stage 1-4: willful violation; national security nexus
tiers.action: DOJ-NSD criminal indictment under IEEPA ($1M per violation); 18 U.S.C. §1832 trade secrets

tiers.name: IEEPA Emergency Order
tiers.trigger: State-sponsored distillation; systemic national security threat
tiers.action: Presidential IEEPA Order blocking transactions; potential secondary sanctions on distillation recipients
